unmapped_findings: The chemical composition of the hot rolled steel was measured to be 10.4 wt.% Mn, 9.7 wt.% Al, 0.70 wt.% C, and Fe balance (b0016).
The measured density of the present (hot rolled) steel is about 6.80 g/cm³, about 13% lower than pure Fe (b0016, b0076).

Lattice parameters obtained from XRD profiles: the lattice parameter of α phase changes in the range 2.89–2.91 Å, of γ phase in the range 3.65–3.67 Å, and of κ-carbide in the range 3.76–3.79 Å (b0027).
The lattices of α and γ phase (the main phase constituents) are slightly expanded by Mn, Al and C atoms, which contributes to the low density of the steel (b0027).
The hot-rolled plate was produced with a thickness of 3 mm, with a finishing rolling temperature around 880 °C, and then water quenched to about 300 °C (b0015).
This hot-rolled + water-quenched plate (HR) is the common precursor/reference state for all subsequent annealing treatments (700–1200 °C for 1 h) studied in the paper (b0015, figure_001).
